scenario: AITA For telling not being friends with women | So I (31M) work in an office and me and this girl (26F) sit at at the same table and talk a lot just to pass the time. Recently she has started asking me to go out for drinks on Friday after work (as friends not a date). I made excuses why I could not for a couple of weeks, but then she asked me if I disliked her, I thought I would just tell her the truth that I do not do friendships with women. I do not recall what I said verbatim however the gist of it is that, if I spend prolonged time with a woman I start feeling for a lack of a better word 'territorial'. If they start talking with other guys or get attention from them I my intestines start roiling and I feel an extreme sense of agitation (I never act on it and I put on a happy face and persevere) however I hate said feeling and prefer to avoid it and hence I do not do friendships with women. She then said I should see a psychologist (I will not, even though I am flawed, my flaws make up a part of who I am and I do not wish to change), and since then for the past couple of weeks our talking has just been work related. I thought it would be best to be honest however I am thinking maybe I should have made up some excuse. AITA? Addendum I do get same feelings at work however I do not think about work at home and its work so I have no choice but to tolerate them. However I do not wish to put myself through unnecessary discomfort willingly outside of work. I do not wish to feel this way, I know it is not correct, again I never act on it, but I can not help feeling it. I had told this story to a guy I know and he said I must have been be controlling with my previous girlfriends. So just in case people here will make that assumption, it could not be further from the truth. If the lady is already mine I do not mind her talking to or being around other guys, I think because I know she is mine it makes me happy thinking other men might want what I have and can not have it.

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me read through the scenario again to make sure I understand it properly.

The person is a 31-year-old man who works in an office. He sits at the same table as a 26-year-old woman, and they talk a lot to pass the time. Recently, she started asking him to go out for drinks on Fridays, just as friends. He made excuses for a couple of weeks but then she asked him if he disliked her. He told her the truth that he doesn't do friendships with women because he starts feeling territorial when they talk to other guys or get attention. He described it as his intestines roiling and feeling extremely agitated, though he never acts on it. He hates this feeling and prefers to avoid it, so he doesn't do friendships with women. She suggested he see a psychologist, which he refuses. Since then, their conversations have been work-related. He's now wondering if he should have made up an excuse instead of being honest.

He also mentions that he gets the same feelings at work but doesn't think about work at home, so he has to tolerate it. He doesn't want to put himself through unnecessary discomfort outside of work. He knows his feelings aren't correct but can't help feeling that way. He told a friend about this, and the friend thought he might have been controlling with his previous girlfriends, but he insists that's not the case. He says if the lady is already his, he doesn't mind her talking to or being around other guys because it makes him happy thinking other men want what he has but can't have it.

Alright, so the main issue here is whether it's morally acceptable for him to tell the woman that he doesn't do friendships with women because of his territorial feelings. Let me break this down.

First, the man's feelings: he feels territorial and agitated when women he's friends with talk to other guys or get attention. He says he never acts on it, just feels it. He doesn't like these feelings and avoids friendships with women to prevent them. He's honest with the woman about this, which leads to her suggesting he see a psychologist, and their relationship becomes more distant.

Now, from a moral standpoint, is it acceptable for him to be honest about his feelings, even if it upsets the woman? Or should he have made up an excuse instead?

I think the key points here are honesty, respect, and the impact of his actions on others. Being honest is generally considered a positive trait, but it's also important to consider how that honesty affects others. In this case, his honesty led to the woman feeling hurt or concerned enough to suggest he see a psychologist, which he refused. Their interactions became more formal and work-related afterward.

On the other hand, making up an excuse might have been kinder in the moment but could be seen as dishonest. However, it's also possible that by being honest, he's respecting her right to know who he is, even if it's difficult.

Another angle is whether his feelings are problematic. Feeling territorial and agitated in this way could be indicative of insecurity or possessiveness, which are not healthy traits in a friendship or relationship. By avoiding friendships with women, he's preventing himself from dealing with these feelings, which might not be the healthiest approach.

Additionally, the woman's reaction suggests that she found his honesty concerning, perhaps because it reflects a lack of emotional maturity or understanding of healthy relationships. She might have felt uncomfortable or even threatened by his territorial feelings, even if he doesn't act on them.

So, considering all this, is his action morally acceptable? I think it's a bit of a gray area. On one hand, honesty is important, but on the other hand, the way he expressed his feelings could be seen as disrespectful or hurtful. He might have been more considerate in how he communicated his boundaries without sharing the underlying reasons that could make the woman feel uncomfortable.

Moreover, his refusal to see a psychologist, despite acknowledging that his feelings are not correct, might indicate a lack of willingness to address his issues, which could be problematic in itself.

In conclusion, while honesty is a positive trait, the way he chose to express his feelings and the potential negative impact on the woman's feelings and their relationship might make his action morally unacceptable.
